analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: USTs head into the FOMC on the back foot, with the 10Y UST yield back above 5% (about 5.02% at time of writing). The overnight move was led by the long end, driven by stronger Australian inflation, higher equities and firmer oil.
The Fed is widely expected to hold. With no new SEP, the reaction will be driven by Warsh's press conference. Mizuho expects a patience-led hawkish hold, not a signal that the inflation job is done.

A clear signal that December remains in play would keep the belly under pressure and terminal pricing elevated. The larger risk is that limited guidance makes the hold sound softer than intended, which would undermine inflation credibility and produce a bear-steepening move.

Oil is a further risk. Reports that Gulf allies were warned to prepare for a possible short, intense US campaign against Iran after the midterms, plus Iran's threat against a South Korean shipowner over Hormuz transits, keep the geopolitical premium in place. Brent is rangebound around $116 per barrel.
DXY continued higher overnight and trades above 102.4. EUR/USD kept falling and trades below 1.1120.

Bunds face crosscurrents from Fed event risk, elevated oil and renewed pressure in EGB spreads. The front end outperformed as December ECB hike pricing eased, with the expected peak falling to 71bp of additional tightening.

Mizuho reads the ECB pricing move as spillover from French financial conditions, not a dovish turn by the ECB. The OAT-Bund spread briefly tested 162bp and is the key pressure point. A negative correlation between French spreads and ECB pricing is expected to persist.

Brent near $116 and a Fed keeping December live limit the room for a sustained rates rally in Europe. Today's EUR5.5bn 10Y Bund auction tests demand, though moves may be contained with the ECB meeting due tomorrow.

Gilts are calm into the Budget, with 10Y yields holding a 5.31-5.35% range. A benign outcome needs fiscal headroom of about GBP12-15bn, a modest rise in the Gilt remit toward GBP249bn and no added pressure on long-end issuance.

Headroom materially below GBP10bn would revive credibility concerns. A larger-than-expected shift away from longs should support ultra-long-end flattening even if the overall remit rises. Mizuho's bias is that the Chancellor delivers a sensible Budget. GBP/USD trades around 1.3275.
Asian equities were risk-on on continued AI optimism. JGBs bear-steepened on a soft 30Y bucket and a bearish tone in USTs. USD/JPY traded in a tight range around 157.90.
Tech earnings from MSFT and GOOGL are due today alongside the FOMC.
earnings_insights: MSFT and GOOGL report earnings today. The note gives no estimates or figures.

tension_points.bull_case: A patience-led hawkish hold with December kept live keeps the belly under pressure and terminal pricing elevated, which is Mizuho's base case.
tension_points.bear_case: Limited guidance makes the hold sound softer than intended, undermining inflation credibility and producing a bear-steepening move.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A clear indication from Warsh at the press conference that December remains in play would confirm the base case. A soft-sounding hold would break it.
